-dur qarin cu ülü odumui : tegün-ü tula bodisug mahasug-nugud-un ülü ebderegci машi <unclear>basa</unclear>
sedkil kemen ügülegdeyü : subudi-a tegün-ü tula bodisug mahasug ene metü uqaju
öber-iyen kiged busud-i medeged ülü getülgeküi-yin tula anggida urbagci sedkil-i
egüskekü bolai : subudi-a ene ber bodisug mahasug-nar-un anggida urbagci sedkil
mön kemen uqagdaqui : subudi-a basa anggida urbagci sedkil-iyer tegüsügsen bodisug
mahasug kemebesü : qamug-i medegci-yin sedkil-i egüskegsen-iyer qamug amitan-u tula
yambar üiledküi kücün-iyer merged-ün cinar-tur oroldun üiledküi kücün-i olugsan bui
bügüdeger qamug-i medegci-yin sedkil-dür dagalduju orogsan-dur medegci-yin sedkil-lüge
selte bolugsan kiged : subudi-a ken qamug-i medegci-yin sedkil-i ülü tebcigci tede
bügüdeger qamug-i medegci-yin sedkil-dür dagalduju orogsan buyu : subudi-a ken sravag-un
gajar kiged bradiyagabud-un gajar-i dotoragcid ber ülü sedkigci tede bügüdeger
qamug-i medegci-yin sedkil-i dagalduju orogsan buyu : subudi-a basa ken qamug-i
medegci-yin sedkil-dür orogsan kiged : <unclear>tegüni</unclear> sedkil-dür ülü sedkigci tede bügüdeger
tegün-i dagalduju orogsan bolai : basa tegün-ü kücün alimad bui tede bügüdeger
merged-ün cinar mön kemen uqagdaqui : subudi-a basa busu ber bodisug mahasug-nar-un
bilig-ün baramid-tur yabuqui cay-tur : alimad jayun minggan-u togan-dur orogsan kiged
caq-lasi ügei togan-dur orogsan bodisug mahasug-nar-tur <unclear>nigen</unclear> sedkil egüskeküi-yin
tedüi-ber ene metü qamug nom-ud-un belges-i üjegülügci kemegdekü diyan-dur
tegüsügül-ün üiledkü buyu : ene metü diyan-dur tegüsügül-ün üiledbesü ber tede
bügüdeger-i öber-ün erke-dür ülü bolgan : tere metü diyan-dur ber ülü sedkimüi :
tegün-ü tula terigülen sedkil egüskeküi-ece inagsida bodisug mahasug-nugud-un
bilig-ün baramid-un tula anggida urbagulugsan mön kemen medegdeküi : subudi-a
basa ene inu bodisug mahasug-nar-un bilig-ün baramid-iyan yambar-iyar öber-tür
edlel-ün tula anggida urbagulju egüskegsen sedkil mön kemen medegdeküi : ::
subudi-a basa bodisug mahasug-nar anggida urbagulugsan-iyar tegüsügsen kemebesü :
ene metü anggida urbagulqui ügei kemen ber ülü sedkiyi : anggida urbagulugsan
mön kemen ber ülü sedkiyi : ene metü ber sedkiged ülü üjegdeküi-yin tula
anggida urbagulugsan sedkil kemen ügülegdeyü :

translation.text:
<meta>continues from previous page: folio 393 (gurba jagun yiren gurba / 三百九十三) of the Peking Kanjur red-ink xylograph of the Perfection of Wisdom in Eight Thousand Lines (Aṣṭasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā, Mongolian: Naiman minggan-tu).</meta>
<warning>Red-ink xylograph print from the Peking Kanjur with areas of faint impression and slight blurring in the middle columns. The OCR contains one Cyrillic character typo ("машi" for "maši") in line 1.</warning>

<margin>The Twenty-Eighth Chapter of the <term>Naiman minggan-tu</term> <gloss>Perfection of Wisdom in Eight Thousand Lines</gloss> .. Three hundred ninety-three</margin>

do not turn back to it either. Therefore, it is called the indestructible, exceedingly <unclear>basa</unclear> mind of the <term>bodisug</term> <gloss>bodhisattva, awakening being</gloss> <term>mahasug</term> <gloss>mahāsattva, great being</gloss>s. O <term>Subudi</term> <gloss>Subhūti, a senior disciple of the Buddha</gloss>, therefore a <term>bodisug</term> <term>mahasug</term>, understanding in this way, generates the <term>anggida urbagci sedkil</term> <gloss>mind of dedication or transformation</gloss> <note>Tibetan: yongs su bsngo ba'i sems; Sanskrit: pariṇāmanā-citta, the mind that redirects merit toward supreme awakening</note> in order to know yet not pass beyond <note>into personal nirvana apart from</note> oneself and others. O <term>Subudi</term>, this should be understood as the <term>anggida urbagci sedkil</term> of the <term>bodisug</term> <term>mahasug</term>s.

O <term>Subudi</term>, furthermore, as for a <term>bodisug</term> <term>mahasug</term> who is endowed with the <term>anggida urbagci sedkil</term>: because they have generated the mind of the <term>qamug-i medegci</term> <gloss>All-Knowing One, omniscience</gloss>, by whatever power of action for the sake of all sentient beings they have attained the power of engaging in the nature of the wise, all of them, upon entering in accordance with the mind of the <term>qamug-i medegci</term>, become endowed with the mind of the Knower. O <term>Subudi</term>, whoever does not abandon the mind of the <term>qamug-i medegci</term>, all of them have entered in accordance with the mind of the <term>qamug-i medegci</term>. O <term>Subudi</term>, whoever does not inwardly entertain thoughts of the level of the <term>sravag</term> <gloss>śrāvaka, hearer-disciple</gloss> or the level of the <term>bradiyagabud</term> <gloss>pratyekabuddha, solitary Buddha</gloss>, all of them have entered following the mind of the <term>qamug-i medegci</term>. O <term>Subudi</term>, furthermore, whoever has entered into the mind of the <term>qamug-i medegci</term>, and does not conceptualize <unclear>tegüni</unclear> in their mind, all of them have entered following it. Furthermore, whatever powers of that mind exist, all of them should be understood as the very nature of the wise.

O <term>Subudi</term>, furthermore, when <term>bodisug</term> <term>mahasug</term>s practice the <term>bilig-ün baramid</term> <gloss>prajñāpāramitā, perfection of wisdom</gloss>, by merely generating a <unclear>nigen</unclear> thought toward <term>bodisug</term> <term>mahasug</term>s who have entered into the count of hundreds of thousands and who have entered into an immeasurable count, they bring to perfection the <term>diyan</term> <gloss>dhyāna, meditative absorption</gloss> called "Revealing the Marks of All Dharmas" <note>Mongolian: qamug nom-ud-un belges-i üjegülügci</note>. Even though they bring such a <term>diyan</term> to perfection, they do not place all those under their own egoistic control, nor do they entertain conceptual thoughts even in such a <term>diyan</term>. Therefore, from the first generation of the mind of awakening onward, it should be known as having been dedicated for the sake of the <term>bilig-ün baramid</term> of the <term>bodisug</term> <term>mahasug</term>s. O <term>Subudi</term>, furthermore, this should be known as the mind generated by turning and dedicating, by whatever means, the <term>bilig-ün baramid</term> of the <term>bodisug</term> <term>mahasug</term>s for one's own spiritual enjoyment.

O <term>Subudi</term>, furthermore, when it is said that <term>bodisug</term> <term>mahasug</term>s are perfected through dedication <note>original: "anggida urbagulugsan"</note>: they do not think, "In this way there is no dedication," nor do they think, "It is indeed dedicated." Because they think in this manner and it is not apprehended <note>as an objective entity</note>, it is called the dedicated mind <note>original: "anggida urbagulugsan sedkil"</note>.

<margin>The Sutra of Various Chapters <note>original: "諸品經", Zhupin jing, the Chinese block-carver's running title used for the Peking Mongolian Kanjur Perfection of Wisdom section</note>, Scroll Twenty-Eight, Upper Part, Three Hundred Ninety-Three</margin>

<summary>Folio 393 of the twenty-eighth chapter of the Mongolian Perfection of Wisdom in Eight Thousand Lines (Naiman minggan-tu) from the Peking Kanjur. In this passage, the Buddha instructs Subhūti on how bodhisattvas cultivate the mind of dedication (anggida urbagci sedkil) directed toward omniscience without clinging to the levels of hearers or solitary Buddhas, and without apprehending the act of dedication itself as a fixed entity.</summary>
